'''Adrian Constantin''' (born 22 April 1970) is a Romanian-Austrian mathematician who does research in the field of nonlinear [[partial differential equations]].<ref name=wien>''[https://mathematik.univie.ac.at/newsevents/nachrichtenvolldarstellung/news/wittgenstein-preis-2020-to-adrian-constantin/?no_cache=1&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&cHash=e45c924514f64aba1123f8681f1bcc20 Wittgenstein Preis 2020 to Adrian Constantin] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200627180349/https://mathematik.univie.ac.at/newsevents/nachrichtenvolldarstellung/news/wittgenstein-preis-2020-to-adrian-constantin/?no_cache=1&tx_news_pi1%5Bcontroller%5D=News&tx_news_pi1%5Baction%5D=detail&cHash=e45c924514f64aba1123f8681f1bcc20 |date=27 June 2020 }}'' Universität Wien: Fakultät für Mathematik, 17 June 2020</ref> He is a professor at the [[University of Vienna]] and has made groundbreaking contributions to the mathematics of wave propagation.<ref name=descopera/> He is listed as an ISI [[Clarivate#Highly Cited Researcher|Highly Cited Researcher]] with more than 160 publications and 11,000 citations.<ref name=wien/>

==Life and career==
Adrian Constantin was born in [[Timișoara]], Romania, where he studied at the [[Nikolaus Lenau High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.descopera.ro/stiinta/19389690-adrian-constantin-matematicianul-roman-care-a-castigat-nobelul-austriei|title=Adrian Constantin, matematicianul român care a câștigat "Nobelul Austriei"|language=ro|first=Mihaela|last=Stoica|date=22 June 2020|website=www.descopera.ro|access-date=28 February 2021}}</ref> He was later educated at the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]] (BSc 1991, MSc 1992) and at [[New York University]] (NYU), where he got his PhD in 1996 under [[Henry McKean]] with the thesis "The Periodic Problem for the [[Camassa–Holm equation]]". He did post-doctoral work at the [[University of Basel]] and at the [[University of Zurich]].<ref name=kings/>

After a short period as a lecturer at the [[Newcastle University|University of Newcastle upon Tyne]], he became a professor at the [[University of Lund]] in 2000, and then was [[Erasmus Smith's Professor of Mathematics]] at [[Trinity College Dublin]] (TCD) from 2004 to 2008, and was made a fellow in 2005.<ref>[https://www.tcd.ie/Secretary/FellowsScholars/2005/index.php Trinity Monday 2005 - Fellows and Scholars]</ref> Since then he has been university professor for partial differential equations at the [[University of Vienna]], and also had a chair at [[King's College London]] during the period 2011–2014.<ref name=kings>''[https://www.kcl.ac.uk/archive/events/nms/Professor-Adrian-Constantin-Inaugural-Lecture Professor Adrian Constantin's Inaugural Lecture]'' King's College London, 23 January 2014</ref>

Constantin specializes in the role of mathematics in geophysics using nonlinear partial differential equations to mathematically model currents and waves in the oceans and in the atmosphere. These flows and waves play an important role in the El Niño climate phenomenon and in natural disasters such as tsunamis.<ref name=witt/> His approach takes into account the fact that the surface of the earth is curved<ref>In most such studies, the Earth is treated as if it were flat.</ref> and the importance of the Coriolis force.<ref name=descopera>''[https://www.descopera.ro/stiinta/19389690-adrian-constantin-matematicianul-roman-care-a-castigat-nobelul-austriei Adrian Constantin, the Romanian mathematician who won the 'Nobel of Austria']'' by Mihaela Stoica, Descoperă România, 22 June 2020 [In Romanian]</ref><ref name=scilog>''[https://scilog.fwf.ac.at/en/environment-and-technology/11820/understanding-earths-system-waves-currents Understanding the Earth’s system of waves and currents] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328200921/https://scilog.fwf.ac.at/en/environment-and-technology/11820/understanding-earths-system-waves-currents |date=28 March 2023 }}'' Alois Pumhösel: SciLogs website</ref>

==Awards and honours==
* 2000: [[Highly Cited Researcher]] with more than 160 publications and 11,000 citations<ref name=wien/>
* 2005: [[Göran Gustafsson Prize]] from the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences<ref name=witt/>
* 2007: [[Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel]] Research Prize from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation<ref name=witt/>
* 2009: Fluid Dynamics Research Prize from the [[Japan Society of Fluid Mechanics]]<ref>[https://www.nagare.or.jp/en/awards.html Awards] The Japan Society of Fluid Mechanics</ref>
* 2010: Advanced Grant from the [[European Research Council]] (ERC)<ref name=ERC>[https://medienportal.univie.ac.at/presse/aktuelle-pressemeldungen/detailansicht/artikel/erc-advanced-grant-fuer-mathematiker-adrian-constantin/ ERC Advanced Grant for Mathematician Adrian Constantin] 17 November 2010, Universität Wien [in German]</ref>
* 2012: Plenary lecture at the European Congress of Mathematicians (ECM) in Krakow<ref name=ECM>[https://www.kcl.ac.uk/archive/news/mathematics/constantineuropeancongress Adrian Constantin Plenary Speaker at European Congress of Mathematics] July 2012, King's College London</ref>
* 2020: [[Wittgenstein Award]] from The Austrian Ministry for Science<ref name=witt>''[https://www.fwf.ac.at/de/news-presse/news/nachricht/nid/20200617-2528/ Mathematician Adrian Constantin named Austria's new Wittgenstein Prize winner] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407070321/https://www.fwf.ac.at/de/news-presse/news/nachricht/nid/20200617-2528/ |date=7 April 2023 }}'' [[Austrian Science Fund]], 17 June 2020</ref>
* 2022: Elected corresponding member of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]], 22 April 2022<ref>[https://www.oeaw.ac.at/news/oeaw-waehlte-45-neue-mitglieder-1 ÖAW elects 45 new members] the Austrian Academy of Sciences, May 3, 2022</ref>
* 2022: Elected member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]], 16 March 2022<ref>[https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/adrian-constantin/ List of Members] German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina</ref>
* 2022: Made an honorary citizen of the city of Timișoara<ref>[https://adevarul.ro/stiri-locale/timisoara/romanul-premiat-cu-nobelul-austriei-a-primit-2210816.html Romanian awarded the "Nobel Prize of Austria" becomes honorary citizen of Timișoara] by Daniel Dancea, [[Adevărul]], Oct 6, 2022</ref> 
* 2024: Elected full member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, 15 April 2024<ref>[https://www.oeaw.ac.at/news/oeaw-waehlt-34-neue-mitglieder ÖAW Elects 34 New Members] Austrian Academy of Sciences, April 15, 2024 </ref>

==Selected publications==
;papers
* 1998: ''Wave breaking for nonlinear nonlocal shallow water equations'' (with J. Escher), [[Acta Mathematica]] 181 229–243.
* 1999: ''A shallow water equation on the circle'' (with [[Henry McKean|H. P. McKean]]), [[Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics|Comm. Pure Appl. Math.]] 52 949–982.
* 2000: ''Stability of peakons'' (with [[Walter A. Strauss|W. Strauss]]), Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 53 603–610.
* 2004: ''Exact steady periodic water waves with vorticity'' (with W. Strauss), Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 57 481–527.
* 2006: ''The trajectories of particles in Stokes waves'', [[Inventiones Mathematicae|Invent. Math.]] 166 523–535.
* 2007: ''Global conservative solutions of the Camassa-Holm equation'' (with A. Bressan), [[Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis|Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal.]] 183 215–239.
* 2011: ''Analyticity of periodic traveling free surface water waves with vorticity'' (with J. Escher), [[Annals of Mathematics|Ann. of Math.]] 173 559–568.
* 2016: ''Global bifurcation of steady gravity water waves with critical layers'' (with W. Strauss and E. Varvaruca), Acta Mathematica 217 195–262.
* 2019: ''Equatorial wave-current interactions'' (with R. I. Ivanov), Comm. Math. Phys. 370 1–48.
* 2022: ''On the propagation of nonlinear waves in the atmosphere'' (with R. S. Johnson), [[Proceedings of the Royal Society|Proceedings of the Royal Society A]] 478 (2260), 20210895
* 2022: ''Stratospheric planetary flows from the perspective of the Euler equation on a rotating sphere'' (with P. Germain), Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., (245 587–644)

;Books
* 2011:  "Nonlinear Water Waves with Applications to Wave-Current Interactions and Tsunamis", [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], Philadelphia, {{ISBN|978-1611971866}}
* 2016:  "Fourier Analysis. Part 1. Theory", [[London Mathematical Society]], Cambridge University Press, {{ISBN|978-1107044104}}
* 2024:  "Analysis I", Springer Spektrum, Berlin, Heidelberg, {{ISBN|978-3-662-68219-7}}
